findings.body: Any label application by a human or a third-party bot re-fires this workflow (`labeled` is subscribed and fires for *any* label — see `docs/TRIGGER_MODES.md:62`), and on that run `scope` emits `matrix=[]`, so this check replaces the previously **green** `Self-review gate` on the same SHA with a **red** one. Concrete sequence: review passes on commit X → teammate triages by adding `bug` → merge is blocked again, and the only unblock is remove + re-add `ready`, i.e. a full paid re-review of an unchanged diff. (The action's own `self-reviewed:*` label is safe — `gh_apply_label` uses the workflow `GITHUB_TOKEN`, which GitHub doesn't recurse runs from — but ordinary triage labels are not.) Consider treating a non-`ready` `labeled` event as satisfied when the PR already carries a review stamp (e.g. check `github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name` for `self-reviewed:*`) instead of failing on the empty matrix.

This rename leaves `README.md:291` still pointing readers at the old title — it quotes and links "Recipe: run once when labelled `ready`, and show Skipped (not green)", which no longer exists as a section name. Update the README link text in this PR so the cross-reference resolves (Rule #7 — docs stay in sync).

Naming collision in the copy-paste recipe: technique 2's decision job is named `gate` (line 80, and line 111 references `needs.gate.outputs.matrix`), while this snippet names the *merge* gate `gate` and expects the decision job to be `gate-decision`. A reader stitching techniques 2 + 3 verbatim gets two jobs named `gate` (invalid workflow). Consider renaming technique 2's decision job to `gate-decision` or adding a one-line note.

summary:
## Verdict

Solid, well-documented fix to a real GitHub gotcha — the gate mechanic itself is correct (fail-closed on scope crash, env-mapped interpolation with no `${{ }}` reaching the shell, per-leg Skipped semantics preserved). Two warnings before merge: the gate can flip red *after* a passing review when any unrelated label is applied, and the recipe rename leaves a stale cross-reference in `README.md`.

## Findings

| # | Severity | File | Summary |
|---|----------|------|---------|
| 1 | ⚠️ warning | `.github/workflows/self-review.yml:237` | Gate flips red when any unrelated label is applied after a passing review, blocking merge until a full paid re-review |
| 2 | ⚠️ warning | `docs/TRIGGER_MODES.md:64` | Recipe rename leaves `README.md:291` referencing a section title that no longer exists |
| 3 | ℹ️ info | `.github/workflows/self-review.yml:218` | Gate job inherits `pull-requests: write` it never needs |
| 4 | ℹ️ info | `docs/TRIGGER_MODES.md:120` | Recipe's technique 2 and technique 3 use colliding job names for different jobs |

## Notes

- **Non-obvious and load-bearing, worth a comment in the workflow:** the design only stays coherent because the action applies `self-reviewed:*` via the workflow's `GITHUB_TOKEN` (`github-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}`), and GitHub does not create new workflow runs from `GITHUB_TOKEN`-triggered events. If a consumer switches to a PAT for `github-token`, the action's own label application re-fires the workflow into an empty-matrix run and the gate goes red moments after turning green. One line in the technique-3 note would spare consumers that trap.
- **Branch-protection flip is manual and unverifiable from the diff.** The gate only works once the dynamic `Self-review — <provider>` names are removed from Required and `Self-review gate` is added — the PR description says to do it; make sure it happens in the same merge window, or the protection momentarily requires checks that no longer exist.
